coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: One Mission Bay
record.summary: One Mission Bay, a completed 350-unit condominium development with ground-floor retail at the corner of 3rd and Channel streets.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- union of a surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint and the boundary of blklot 8715007, a RETIRED DataSF parcel (active false; mapped 2014-02-11, dropped 2016-11-16; last Assessor roll 2017, property location 110 Channel St), not a hand trace or plan estimate -- the shape therefore includes a superseded boundary, and whether to keep it has not been decided. The per-unit condo lots were not identified in a September 2026 check (no active lot in DataSF Parcels carries mapblklot 8715007), and no single per-unit blklot represents the whole building so the building cannot be mapped from a single Assessor parcel the way a single-owner building can; blklot 8715007, a retired parcel, is the exception used here. Real-geometry-without-a-single-owner-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 563104192, name=One Mission Bay), unioned with the boundary of retired DataSF parcel blklot 8715007

milestones.text: One Mission Bay (110 Channel St/1000 3rd St) completed (Strada's project page: 'completed in 2018'; no month given)

changes.text: The map caveat and notes called blklot 8715007 a current common-area/master lot with no address. DataSF Parcels shows it as a retired parcel (mapped 2014-02-11, dropped 2016-11-16) whose last Assessor roll is 2017 with the address 110 Channel St, and no active lot carries it as its map block-lot, so the caveat and a dated note now say the map shape includes a superseded boundary (the shape itself was not changed). The notes also now say that '13 stories', a '6-story perimeter building', CIM Group as developer and Arquitectonica as architect appear in no cited source (Compass says 16 stories, OpenStreetMap 17, Strada 'partnered with the buyer'). The notes now cite Strada's 350 units and 20,000 sq ft of retail and the Compass pool and concierge, dropping unit sizes and other amenities. The June 2018 completion milestone now reads 2018, and the November 2016 topping-out milestone (cited only to Business Wire's home page; the release could not be read) was removed. The map's source description now mentions that the shape joins in the retired parcel's boundary.

open_questions: This record was created on 2026-09-27 to host Pier & Point's own field photos. Its summary is limited to what its cited source was re-read to confirm that day; fuller details given in this record's other notes (developer, architect, unit count, year built) were left out of the summary where that source didn't state them. Not yet researched: no milestones, costs or facts.
record.notes: 350 condominium units across two connected structures (a high-rise tower plus a lower perimeter building) at 1000 3rd St and 110 Channel St; Strada's project page lists 350 units and 20,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, and the Compass building page lists a pool and concierge (other amenities and the 495-1,528 sq ft unit sizes are not confirmed by any cited page). A claimed ~50,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail could not be confirmed as specific to this building -- not asserted here. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
